regimens.indication: Skin/Skin Structure, Intra-Abdominal, and Gynecological Infections (Ampicillin-Sulbactam) — Adults

refs.quote: Ampicillin and Sulbactam for Injection is indicated for the treatment of infections due to susceptible strains of the designated microorganisms in the conditions listed below. Skin and Skin Structure Infections
The recommended adult dosage of Ampicillin and Sulbactam for Injection is 1.5 g (ampicillin 1 g and sulbactam 0.5 g) to 3 g (ampicillin 2 g and sulbactam 1 g) every six hours.

dose.frequency: every 6 hours (1.5 g to 3 g q6h; max sulbactam 4 g/day)

regimens.dose_text: 1.5 g (1 g ampicillin + 0.5 g sulbactam) to 3 g (2 g ampicillin + 1 g sulbactam) IV every 6 hours by slow IV injection over 10–15 min or IV infusion over 15–30 min. Total sulbactam dose should not exceed 4 g/day.

regimens.indication: Skin/Skin Structure, Intra-Abdominal, and Gynecological Infections (Ampicillin-Sulbactam) — Adults (Intramuscular)

refs.quote: Intra-Abdominal Infections caused by beta-lactamase producing strains of Escherichia coli , Klebsiella spp. (including K. pneumoniae * ) , Bacteroides spp. (including B. fragilis ), and Enterobacter spp.* Gynecological Infections

Ampicillin and Sulbactam for Injection may be administered by deep intramuscular injection (see DIRECTIONS FOR USE-Preparation for Intramuscular Injection section). The recommended adult dosage of Ampicillin and Sulbactam for Injection is 1.5 g (ampicillin 1 g and sulbactam 0.5 g) to 3 g (ampicillin 2 g and sulbactam 1 g) every six hours.

dose.frequency: every 6 hours (1.5 g to 3 g deep IM q6h; max sulbactam 4 g/day)

regimens.dose_text: 1.5 g (1 g ampicillin + 0.5 g sulbactam) to 3 g (2 g ampicillin + 1 g sulbactam) by deep IM injection every 6 hours. Total sulbactam dose should not exceed 4 g/day.

regimens.indication: Susceptible Bacterial Infections (Ampicillin-Sulbactam) — Pediatrics (1 year of age or older, < 40 kg)

refs.quote: Pediatric Patients 1 Year of Age or Older: The recommended daily dose of Ampicillin and Sulbactam for Injection in pediatric patients is 300 mg per kg of body weight administered via intravenous infusion in equally divided doses every 6 hours.
The course of intravenous therapy should not routinely exceed 14 days.

dose.frequency: every 6 hours (300 mg/kg/day total; 200 mg ampicillin + 100 mg sulbactam/kg/day)

regimens.dose_text: 300 mg/kg/day (200 mg ampicillin + 100 mg sulbactam per kg/day) IV infusion in equally divided doses every 6 hours (75 mg/kg q6h). IM route not established in pediatrics; IV course should not routinely exceed 14 days.

refs.quote: Pediatric patients weighing 40 kg or more should be dosed according to adult recommendations, and the total dose of sulbactam should not exceed 4 g per day.

dose.frequency: every 6 hours (1.5 g to 3 g q6h; max sulbactam 4 g/day)

regimens.dose_text: Pediatric patients >= 40 kg: Dose according to adult recommendations — 1.5 g to 3 g IV every 6 hours; total sulbactam dose should not exceed 4 g/day.

value.effect: Concurrent administration of allopurinol and ampicillin substantially increases the incidence of erythematous and maculopapular skin rashes.
value.management: Monitor for cutaneous hypersensitivity; consider alternative antimicrobial therapy if rash develops.

refs.quote: The concurrent administration of allopurinol and ampicillin increases substantially the incidence of rashes in patients receiving both drugs as compared to patients receiving ampicillin alone.

value.effect: Probenecid competitively blocks renal tubular secretion of ampicillin and sulbactam, elevating and prolonging serum antibiotic concentrations.
value.management: This interaction is sometimes utilized intentionally to achieve higher tissue/CSF levels; monitor for dose-dependent neurotoxicity.

refs.quote: Probenecid decreases the renal tubular secretion of ampicillin and sulbactam. Concurrent use of probenecid with ampicillin and sulbactam for injection may result in increased and prolonged blood levels of ampicillin and sulbactam.
The concurrent administration of allopurinol and ampicillin increases substantially the incidence of rashes in patients receiving both drugs as compared to patients receiving ampicillin alone.
